tasks.short: Review supplier performance, discuss forecasts, and agree improvement actions.

steps.what: Retrieve supplier delivery, shortage, and quality records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Retrieve purchase commitments and material forecasts from the {ERP}.
Reconcile exports and calculate supplier measures in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare the supplier review pack in the {DOCS}.
Discuss performance, challenge explanations, and negotiate recovery actions with the supplier.
Turn meeting notes into minutes and an action log in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Manager's meeting notes and proposed commitments.
loop.output: Draft minutes and actions with owners, dates, and supporting note references.
loop.check: Check names and dates; distinguish proposals from agreements; manager checks disputed wording.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per meeting; unresolved statements remain flagged for manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes express commitments inconsistently; templates cannot reliably identify agreement.

steps.what: Approve and send supplier minutes through {EMAIL}, confirming commitments and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations join {OPS_SYSTEM} performance records with {ERP} commitments on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, feeding a {BI} scorecard and a templated review pack in the {DOCS}. A bounded loop turns manager notes into draft actions; a configured {WORKFLOW} sends the approved follow-up through {EMAIL} and tracks due dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier identifiers and metric definitions differ across records. Meeting outcomes arrive as informal notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, reusable joins, document templates, and faster coding lower implementation effort. A bounded extraction loop handles the notes.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed delivery measures, confidential forecasts, and supplier leverage still require judgement. GDPR applies to named contacts and meeting records.
tasks.human_edge: Read hesitation, distinguish excuses from genuine constraints, and negotiate commitments the supplier can meet.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery-plan adjustments for critical suppliers.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding packs and more time testing recovery commitments. Existing commercial authority remains unchanged; more frequent interventions fit within that authority.

reach.task: Estimate the transport and inventory cost of a supplier recovery proposal.
reach.learn: Cost-to-serve modelling, expedite costs, and uncertainty ranges.

evidence.claim: Structured supplier measures, templated packs, and reminders can use deterministic technology; the conversation remains human.
The proposed effort shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Today, operational records and forecasts are reconciled in a workbook before supplier meetings.
Shares estimate active task effort, including preparation and follow-up; they exclude waiting.
The design uses manager notes and does not require meeting recording.
Access estimates cover supplier-contact data review and national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Which supplier identifiers and delivery definitions are authoritative?
Which forecast details may be disclosed to each supplier?
Who may commit to changed quantities, dates, or commercial terms?
Which exports, interfaces, and approval features are available?
research_questions: Does the existing {PROCUREMENT} already provide suitable scorecards and action tracking?
Can disputed deliveries be traced to receipt-level evidence?
How accurately can note extraction distinguish proposed and accepted commitments?
new_work: Resolve unmatched suppliers and disputed metric records.
Review extracted commitments before external sending.
Maintain metric definitions, connector mappings, and reminder rules.

tasks.short: Monitor demand forecasts and quotas, assess supply effects, and recommend responses.

steps.what: Retrieve current and previous demand forecasts from the {ERP}.
Retrieve stock, capacity, and production quotas from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Align item codes, periods, and units in the {SPREADSHEET}; investigate mismatches.
Calculate forecast changes, shortages, and capacity scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess scenario credibility and select issues requiring intervention.
Discuss demand assumptions and response options with planning and commercial colleagues.
Publish the reviewed planning brief in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Use scenario functions in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with governed {ERP} inputs and reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A {BI} view exposes forecast changes, shortage dates, capacity constraints, and assumptions; a template in the {DOCS} publishes the manager's reviewed response without changing operational plans.
tasks.previous_blocker: Period alignment, item mappings, and inconsistent assumptions made recurring analysis expensive. Scenario tools often existed without reliable joined inputs.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured planning functions and reusable reconciliation code can produce repeatable scenarios. Faster coding reduces the cost of connecting existing data.
tasks.still_hard: Promotions, demand shocks, capacity losses, and stale lead times can invalidate plausible calculations. Predictive accuracy must be checked after outcomes arrive.
tasks.human_edge: Question demand assumptions and balance service, cash, and operational resilience when scenarios disagree.
tasks.altitude: The manager reviews changes and scenario assumptions instead of assembling recurring workbooks. No new spending or allocation authority is assumed.

reach.task: Translate a selected shortage response into a feasible material and production schedule.
reach.learn: Time fences, material requirements, bottleneck capacity, and schedule stability.

evidence.claim: Slim4 provides inventory forecasting and stock-setting capabilities.
The Lasaulec vendor case reports lower stock with high availability; it does not establish this proposal's expected outcome.
Joining structured planning data and calculating scenarios do not inherently require a language model.
Effort shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Quotas mean production targets or supply allocations, not individual employee targets.
The {OPS_SYSTEM} has configurable planning functions adequate for the initial scenarios.
Today, a workbook joins forecast and operational data.
Testing includes historical forecast snapshots and a live comparison period.
The design does not score employees; access and national consultation requirements still need checking.
unknowns: What does quota mean in this operation?
Are forecast versions and historical assumptions retained?
Which constraints can the existing planning functions represent?
Who can approve production, purchasing, or allocation changes?
How current and reliable are stock, capacity, and lead-time records?
research_questions: Can existing planning configuration replace workbook calculations before custom code is built?
Which alert thresholds identify actionable changes without overwhelming planners?
How well do historical scenarios predict actual shortage timing?
new_work: Resolve mapping, freshness, and unit exceptions.
Maintain scenario assumptions and alert thresholds.
Compare predicted effects with actual outcomes and investigate persistent errors.

tasks.short: Coordinate material and production transitions for engineering changes, product extensions, and launches.

steps.what: Review the engineering change package in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Versioned engineering change package and launch requirements.
loop.output: Draft transition requirements with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate item identifiers and revisions; manager checks effectivity, dependencies, and missing requirements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per package; conflicting revisions or missing effectivity go to engineering.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative change instructions and attachments contain requirements beyond standard form fields.

steps.what: Check affected materials, open orders, and bills of materials in the {ERP}.
Check stock locations, work in progress, and production capacity in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Build the runout, replenishment, and cutover plan in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve dependencies and negotiate transition responsibilities with engineering, purchasing, quality, and production.
Approve cutover conditions and record the release decision in the {DOCS}.
Release approved material and order changes in the {ERP}.
Monitor transition exceptions and material flow in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: A configured {PROJECT} transition template links requirements in the {DOCS} to exposure checks from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; a bounded loop extracts narrative requirements for review. Deterministic calculations propose runout and cutover options, while a {WORKFLOW} requires release approval and a checked change set before updating the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change packages, material exposure, and action ownership sit in separate records. Revision changes make copied plans unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned records, dependency templates, and deterministic exposure calculations can be connected at lower development cost. Bounded extraction reduces document-reading effort.
tasks.still_hard: Physical stock can differ from records, and engineering effectivity can be ambiguous. Safe cutover depends on quality evidence and coordinated execution.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicting priorities, secure realistic commitments, and judge whether the organisation is ready to switch.

ambition.what: Material-obsolescence exposure checks before design freeze.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time challenging transition risks before launch and less time chasing status. Release and engineering decision rights remain with their designated approvers.

reach.task: Maintain cross-functional launch dependencies and escalate threats to the critical path.
reach.learn: Dependency modelling, change control, and milestone risk.

reach.task: Define the evidence needed to release a changed material or process.
reach.learn: Traceability, acceptance criteria, and controlled revision handling.

evidence.claim: Dependency templates, exposure calculations, version checks, and approval workflows can support engineering transitions deterministically.
Narrative requirement extraction needs source checks and does not establish engineering correctness.
Effort shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates; the digest supplies no matching transition case.

assumptions: The representative operation manufactures or assembles products.
Engineering packages are versioned and affected item identifiers can be resolved.
Shares cover active handling across the coordinated task, excluding approval waiting.
The engineering manager is the assumed release authority; actual governance may require several sign-offs.
Access estimates include segregation-of-duties review and national consultation where changed working arrangements require it.
unknowns: Who owns engineering revisions and cutover approval?
Are lot, serial, and work-in-progress records reliable enough for automated exposure checks?
Can the {ERP} validate and stage changes before posting?
Which supplier or customer approvals constrain a transition?
Which staff consultation and access processes apply?
research_questions: Can existing {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW} configuration replace the current transition workbook?
How are stale approvals invalidated when requirements or quantities change?
Which updates support safe retries and which require manual execution?
Can a past transition validate exposure calculations and exception routing?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and unresolved revision conflicts.
Maintain transition templates and evidence requirements.
Handle failed updates, reconcile partial changes, and verify physical exceptions.
Keep approvals tied to the exact change-set version.

tasks.short: Find and qualify suppliers with purchasing, engineering, and quality colleagues.

steps.what: Agree capability, capacity, quality, and commercial requirements with relevant departments.
Search supplier directories using a supplier discovery service in {OTHER}.

loop.input: Approved directory exports and referrals, with qualification criteria.
loop.output: Candidate shortlist with criterion matches, gaps, and source references.
loop.check: Apply hard filters in code; verify each suggested capability against its cited source.
loop.stop: Process one supplied candidate batch with one correction pass; unsupported candidates require manual research.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier descriptions use varied terminology; exact filters miss relevant capabilities.

steps.what: Request qualification evidence and clarify supplier interest through {EMAIL}.
Review certificates, questionnaires, and technical evidence in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Submitted certificates, questionnaire answers, and technical documents.
loop.output: Evidence matrix with source passages, dates, scope, and missing items.
loop.check: Validate required fields and expiry dates; specialist verifies authenticity, scope, and conflicting claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per evidence pack; unreadable or unsupported evidence remains unverified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents vary in structure and wording; rules alone cannot locate all relevant evidence.

steps.what: Inspect supplier facilities and test claimed capabilities where qualification requires a visit.
Compare findings and agree a qualification recommendation across departments.
Approve qualification status and conditions in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Notify the supplier of the decision and conditions through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure qualification stages, evidence requests, conditions, and approvals in the {PROCUREMENT}, linked to controlled evidence in the {DOCS}. Bounded loops suggest candidates from approved directory exports and prepare cited evidence matrices; a {WORKFLOW} routes gaps and sends reviewed notices through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier evidence arrives in varied formats, while departments apply partly tacit criteria. No shared view reliably separates missing evidence from a failed requirement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing qualification workflows can hold the records and approvals. Bounded document extraction makes evidence comparison cheaper without delegating qualification decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Certificates can be misleading, site capability can differ from claims, and commercial dependence affects risk tolerance. GDPR applies to personal data in supplier records.
tasks.human_edge: Test credibility, reconcile technical and commercial trade-offs, and decide which risks can be accepted with conditions.

ambition.what: Small suppliers needing guided qualification evidence submission.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time investigating capability and developing alternatives, with less evidence chasing. Qualification and spending authority remain with the designated decision makers.

reach.task: Design supplier audit criteria and corrective-action closure requirements.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, audit sampling, certificate scope, and risk-based qualification.

reach.task: Assess whether an alternative supplier reduces disruption exposure.
reach.learn: Shared upstream dependencies, recovery times, and geographic concentration.

evidence.claim: Qualification records, evidence checklists, expiry checks, and approval routing can use existing configuration and deterministic rules.
Cited document extraction can support review but cannot establish supplier capability or certificate authenticity.
Effort shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates; the digest supplies no matching supplier-qualification case.

assumptions: The representative case requires substantive technical qualification and a supplier visit.
Low-risk suppliers use a shorter path when policy permits; required verification is retained.
Approved directory exports are available; the design does not require autonomous browsing.
The procurement manager is the assumed final approver, supported by technical and quality sign-offs.
Access work includes supplier-data permissions and national consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which supplier categories require visits, samples, or independent checks?
Who approves qualification and accepts conditional risks?
Which directory sources permit export and reuse?
Can the {PROCUREMENT} enforce qualification conditions before ordering?
What support would help small suppliers provide equivalent evidence?
research_questions: Which existing qualification features can be configured before building custom records?
Can criterion wording be made explicit enough for consistent evidence review?
How often does extraction omit a material qualification restriction?
Can conditional approval and evidence expiry automatically restrict purchasing?
new_work: Review candidate matches and unsupported capability claims.
Verify evidence authenticity and resolve contradictions.
Maintain qualification criteria, document mappings, and expiry rules.
Help suppliers resolve evidence gaps and track conditional approvals.

role.altitude: The supply chain manager's week shifts toward supplier recovery, scenario assessment, transition readiness, and capability checks. Administrative effort falls, while existing commercial, engineering, and qualification approvals remain explicit.
reach: Work with logistics analysts on the cost and service effects of recovery options.
Work with production planning clerks on feasible shortage responses and cutovers.
Work with quality control systems managers on qualification evidence and release conditions.
Work with business continuity planners on supplier concentration and recovery exposure.
skills_to_grow: Define operational measures and trace them to source records.
Interpret scenario uncertainty and test assumptions against outcomes.
Review extracted evidence without treating fluent text as verification.
Design exception routes, approval boundaries, and version controls.
Negotiate realistic cross-functional and supplier commitments.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring supply-risk review that connects forecast changes, supplier recovery, launch exposure, and qualified alternatives. Recommend specific interventions with traceable evidence; obtain any expanded decision rights through an explicit management mandate.
